To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the variances of all the components of the analysis of variance can be expressed as linear functions of the variances of certain linear combinations of the observations.
, for balanced designs, the variances of variance components are expressible as functions of the variance components themselves.
the variances of estimates of variance components are equal to their squares divided by the number of degrees of freedom for that component.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following problem.
the problem of estimating the variances of variance components.
the estimation of the components of variance in the analysis of variance situation, where we have assumed that the observations are normally and independently distributed.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the variances of variance components are not affected by the removal of the assumption of normality.

the estimates are not only unbiased but also are the best linear unbiased estimates of their parameters, and that the variance of each of them is inversely related to the number of degrees of freedom of its source.

, in the case of a balanced design, if we are willing to assume that the variances of all of the quantities in the analysis of variance situation are finite (which we must do in order to have any variance estimates at all), then we can obtain estimates of the variances of these quantities which have smaller variances than the corresponding natural estimates.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we can obtain unbiased estimators for variance components in a balanced situation, even when the population distributions are nonnormal, but that these estimates are no longer independent, so that we cannot use them in the usual ways to make tests of significance or to obtain confidence intervals.
the variance of the natural estimate of a variance component is a function of the variance components themselves.
the variances of estimates of variance components are, in general, functions of the variance components themselves.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the variance of the estimate of any variance component is proportional to the sum of the squares of the corresponding mean squares, and that the variance of any mean square is proportional to the corresponding mean square.
the variance of an estimate of a variance component is a polykay in the variance component, and this polykay has a simple structure which is easy to remember.
the variance of the variance component estimator can be expressed as the product of the variance of the mean of the appropriate polykay and the square of the variance of a single observation.
